input.quote: Array shall not require Ono to place orders directly with a Subcontractor if such Subcontractor is unwilling to fulfill such orders on terms as favorable to Ono as the terms such Subcontractors have extended to Array.
input.rationale: Searches for MFN-style language ("most favorable/favored", "no less favorable", "best price", "match", "at least as favorable") and a read of the payments (Art. VI), payments/books-and-records (Art. VII) and certain covenants (Art. VIII) articles show no undertaking by Ono (our party) to extend to Array any better terms granted to third parties or to match third-party offers. The only comparable-terms language, Section 9.2(b) (p0502), runs in our favour: Array cannot force Ono to order Materials directly from a Subcontractor unless that Subcontractor offers Ono terms as favourable as those extended to Array. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer; MFN-type protection in Customer's favour is welcome), so no redline is proposed. Note that Art. VIII does contain exclusivity/non-compete covenants on Ono (Section 8.2), but those are a distinct commercial term and not an MFN/best-terms undertaking.
